frequency_question: What proportion of major complex legislative overhauls clear all required procedural stages and are signed into law within a 42-day calendar window?
membership_rule: Includes major structural reform bills initiated or finalized and passed in a single short legislative burst (e.g., lame-duck or emergency sessions); excludes routine appropriations and non-controversial technical corrections.

cases.name: TARP / Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008
American Taxpayer Relief Act of 2012 (Fiscal Cliff)

provenance_note: 6 cases named, 18 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (3.0x)
coverage_note: 6 named hits; estimated 12 misses where compressed major reform bills failed to clear both chambers and secure signature within a 42-day window.
known_gaps: Exact count of failed legislative vehicle attempts in late-session or crisis windows is subject to varying definitions of 'major structural reform'.
skeleton: Total emergency/lame-duck major structural packages passing final legislative steps within 6 weeks since 1994 divided by total attempted major legislative pushes in compressed windows.
multiplier: 6 successful high-speed major legislative enactments out of 18 attempted major compressed packages identified in modern congressional history.
validity_reason: Congressional rules, filibuster dynamics, and bicameral friction change slowly across decades, remaining stable through multiple electoral cycles.
